title: The Gospel Crossover
theme: The collision of the church and the charts in the 1990s, featuring the artists, producers, and labels that blurred the lines between secular R&B and contemporary gospel
narrativePurpose: Test the player's knowledge of the roots of 90s R&B vocal styling and the specific crossover moments that dominated mainstream radio
toneProgression: Massive secular hits with church origins → Crossover production history → Label origins and obscure group rosters

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 1-9-9-7 — the year Kirk Franklin's Stomp featuring God's Property crossed out of gospel radio and onto the pop mainstream. The year the church finally took a chart position.

questions.question: Kirk Franklin's landmark crossover album 'The Nu Nation Project' — released in 1998 — was released on which independent gospel label?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — NU NATION'S HOME LABEL

metadata.fact: Kirk Franklin's 'The Nu Nation Project' was released on GospoCentric Records — the independent label that was home to his earlier work including 'Kirk Franklin & The Family' (1993) and 'Whatcha Lookin' 4' (1996). GospoCentric was distributed through Interscope and was the primary vehicle for gospel music crossing into the mainstream in the 1990s.
metadata.storyHook: GospoCentric was the label that made it possible for gospel to reach secular radio. Kirk Franklin used it to build the bridge.

metadata.fact: 'Count on Me' — performed by Whitney Houston and CeCe Winans — appeared on the Waiting to Exhale soundtrack (1995). The song won the Grammy Award for Best Gospel Performance by a Duo, Group, Choir or Chorus at the 38th Grammy Awards in 1996.
metadata.storyHook: Whitney Houston and CeCe Winans brought gospel to a mainstream soundtrack audience in 1995. The Grammys noticed.

reserve.question: Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men's 'One Sweet Day' — which topped the Billboard Hot 100 for 16 consecutive weeks — appeared on which Mariah Carey album?

metadata.fact: 'One Sweet Day' appeared on Mariah Carey's fifth studio album 'Daydream,' released in October 1995. The song was written as a tribute to loved ones who had passed away. It spent 16 consecutive weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — a record that stood until 2019.
metadata.storyHook: Daydream carried the most successful collaboration in Hot 100 history. A record that stood for over two decades.
metadata.sourceNotes: Official CD liner notes for Daydream (Columbia). Billboard Hot 100 historical data.

questions.question: Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis founded Perspective Records — the gospel and inspirational imprint that launched Sounds of Blackness — as a joint venture with which major label?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 3 OF 3 — SOUNDS OF BLACKNESS'S LABEL

metadata.fact: Perspective Records was founded by Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis as a joint venture with A&M Records — giving their gospel and inspirational imprint the distribution power of a major label while maintaining creative independence. It was the vehicle through which Sounds of Blackness reached a mainstream audience.
metadata.storyHook: Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis didn't just produce the music. They built the label to release it. A&M backed the whole operation.
metadata.sourceNotes: PRIORITY VERIFY: Confirm Perspective Records was a joint venture between Jimmy Jam/Terry Lewis and A&M Records. Must be sourced before production.
